Definition: to break out (in many applications, direct and indirect, literal and figurative)
BiblicalUsage: Parats means to break out, to break through, to burst forth. The name of Perez comes from it, when Tamar's son breaks forth first in Genesis 38:29, and David names the place Baal-perazim in 1 Chronicles 14:11, saying God has broken in upon his enemies like the breaking forth of waters. In 1 Samuel 3:1 the word runs the other way: the word of the Lord was precious, and there was no open vision, no breaking forth of revelation. Psalm 80:12 laments that God has broken down the vineyard's hedges.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God breaks through where He pleases, in blessing and in judgment alike: the waters break over David's enemies, the silence breaks over Samuel's childhood, and the hedge breaks around a vineyard that has forgotten its keeper. I hold that the breach He makes is never aimless: it opens a way for His people, or it opens a way for His judgment, and either way it is His hand that breaks through.
